title: Verity Auctions — Ottmar Auction Service
description: Dean Ottmar types the sale bill on the office machine, scans it, photographs the lots himself, and posts what everything brought afterward. Four other sites copy the bills and get the dates wrong.

regions.name: Milbrook, Kerrin and the north end

listings.title: Ottmar Auction Service — who runs this and what it is
listings.body:
Dean Ottmar, auctioneer. State license AU-1187, first issued 1992, renewed in every even year since at the state office, by check.

I sell household goods, farm machinery, shop tools and occasionally real estate, on the order of the owner, the executor or the court. I work New Carrow, Halsey, Coyne Flats, Marchfield, Gridfall, Ashkettle, Milbrook and the north end. I have gone outside the county eleven times and would rather not.

This site is me. I type the bill on the machine in the office, scan it, and photograph the lots with a camera on a tripod in whatever light is in the building. If a photograph is crooked, the camera was crooked. If a scan has a staple shadow on it, there was a staple.

There is no app. There is no mailing list. I do not sell your address because I do not write it down.

I have never taken a bid over the internet and I am not set up to.

Office: 555-0221. The office is the pole barn behind the house on Grange Road, New Carrow. Somebody answers between eight and six most days and it is either me or Jeanette.

Anything you receive telling you this license is about to be suspended is a lie. The state does not send those and would not know my email if they did.

listings.title: Terms of sale — these apply to every sale unless the bill says otherwise
listings.body:
[b]Payment.[/b] Cash or good check with photo identification. Out of county checks require a bank letter of guarantee brought to the sale, not mailed after it. Cards are run through a machine that takes its cut whether I like it or not.

[b]Buyer's premium.[/b] 10 percent. 3 percent of that comes back for cash or check.

[b]Registration.[/b] Bidder numbers are issued at the clerk's table from 8:30. Driver's license required. The number is yours for the day and what is bought on it is yours.

[b]As is, where is.[/b] Everything sells as it sits. Nothing is tested unless the bill says tested. Serial numbers are read off the plate and I read them wrong sometimes.

[b]Announcements.[/b] Announcements made from the block on the day of the sale take precedence over this page, over the printed bill, and over anything any other website says about my sale.

[b]Settlement.[/b] Settle at the clerk's table before you load. Nothing leaves the premises until it is paid for.

[b]Removal.[/b] Small items day of sale. Machinery by the Wednesday following at 5:00. After that it is stored at your cost. Twice I have had to sell the same item a second time and both times the second price was lower.

[b]Not responsible.[/b] Not responsible for accidents on the premises or for items after they are sold. Watch where you put your feet in a barn.

I am the agent of the seller. I am not the seller, and I do not warrant anything.

listings.title: If you have not been to a sale before
listings.body:
People ask, so.

Come at 8:30 and look at everything you might bid on, with your hands. The preview is the only free part of the day and it is the part that decides what you pay.

Get a number. You do not have to use it.

I start with boxes and smalls off the wagon at 10:00 because that is when people are standing there. Tools around 11:00. On a farm sale the machinery sells after dinner, usually 1:00, and the bill says approximate and means it.

Two rings run on a big sale. One is me and one is whoever I have hired that week. Listen for which ring is selling what, because they are eighty feet apart and both of them are loud.

Bid by raising your hand, your number, or your chin. I will find you. You cannot buy a corn planter by scratching your ear. That is a story auctioneers tell about themselves.

If you buy a box lot you have bought the whole box, including the part under the newspaper, and you take it with you.

Bring cash for lunch. The people selling lunch are not me and they are not taking a card.

listings.title: Absentee and telephone bids
listings.body:
I take an absentee bid on a specific lot number, in writing, at the office, by the Thursday before the sale.

I do not take one on "the furniture" or "anything old" or "whatever you think."

I execute it competitively. That means I bid it up only as far as I have to. If you leave $200 on a lot, it opens at $40 and nobody else wants it, you own it at $45 and I will tell you so.

Telephone bidding on machinery only, only if I know you, and only if you call the week before so your number is written on the card in front of me and not typed into something that has to be logged into.

Tie between two absentee bids goes to the one that arrived first. I date them when Jeanette hands them to me and she has never been wrong about a date.

listings.title: My sales listed on other sites are not listed by me
listings.body:
Four sites copy my bills. None of them asked. One of them wrote to ask and I did not answer, which I suppose is my share of it.

What they have wrong this month:

[list][*]One has the Toomey sale on Sunday. It is Saturday. The bill has said Saturday since the 2nd and the bill is a scan of a piece of paper.[*]One has moved the Brawner farm to Gridfall. It is on Brill Road in Nye Mills township, twenty-two miles out, and the difference between those two addresses is your whole morning.[*]One is still showing the Ledbetter sale from August as upcoming. That sale is over. The results are on this site.[*]One describes the Brawner farm as being near the site of the 2004 Gridfall substation fire, caused by lightning. The fire was 2003, it was at Depot and Quarry Road in Gridfall, and the state commission put it down to insulation gone with age. None of that is any of my business except the part where it is printed over the top of my sale bill. It is on the county wiki and has been for years: [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/wiki/substation-fire-2003]substation fire, 2003[/url].[/list]

Two of them post the copy on to [url=synth://gridline.social/]Gridline[/url], where a third thing writes a summary of the copy and a fourth thing replies to the summary. I read one of those threads all the way to the bottom. There was not a person in it.

If a date you saw somewhere does not match the bill on this page, the bill on this page is right. I typed it.

Ronnie Pelt runs the notices at [url=synth://gridfall-buysell.net/]gridfall-buysell.net[/url] and types my bills off the paper copy I hand him. He has telephoned me twice about a line that looked wrong. Both times he was right and I changed it. Nobody else has ever telephoned me about anything.

listings.title: Lunch, toilets, and where to park
listings.body:
Lunch at the Toomey sale is the ladies of [url=synth://stmarks-verity.org/]St Mark's[/url]. Lunch at the Brawner sale is the Kerrin Ambulance Auxiliary. Both do a sandwich, a hot dish and pie, both start at 11:00, and both are done by 1:30. Pay them, not me.

Portable toilet on site at every sale. One at a household sale, two at a farm sale, three at Brawner because there will be four hundred people in that yard and only one lane out of it.

Park where the man with the flag puts you. He is not being unreasonable. He is thinking about the hay wagon that has to come out at 1:00 and about the ambulance if it has to come in.

Do not park on Brill Road. The township grader uses it and so does the milk truck, and the milk truck does not stop for an auction.

Saturday, October 17, 2026, 9:00 a.m.
[url=synth://newcarrowgrange.synth/]New Carrow Grange hall[/url], Grange Road. Inside if it rains, in the lot if it does not.

Take-in Thursday October 15, 1:00 to 6:00, and Friday October 16, 9:00 to 4:00. Nothing accepted the morning of the sale, and I mean that one.

What is in so far: two wagon loads of shop tools, a pallet of cast iron, a run of blue jars, four hundred feet of good lumber, a pedal tractor, a gun cabinet, six dining chairs that are not from my thirty-one, and a box of railroad paperwork somebody found in a shed on Depot Street.

The railroad box has waybills in it. Two men from [url=synth://forums.verityrail.org/]the rail forum[/url] have already asked what is in it. What is in it is waybills.

Smalls first, tools at about 10:30, lumber and the big items last.

[b]Commission[/b], paid by the consignor out of the proceeds: 25 percent under $50, 15 percent from $50 to $500, 10 percent over $500. Nothing at all on a lot under $5 because I put those in a box and sell the box.

[b]Terms[/b] as posted. Cash or good check with photo identification. Everything sells. Nothing here is subject to a reserve and I will not take one on a consignment sale.

listings.title: SELF STORAGE LIEN SALE — Thursday October 22, 10:00 a.m. — Ashkettle industrial estate — 9 units
listings.body:
[b]LIEN SALE, SELF STORAGE[/b]
Thursday, October 22, 2026, 10:00 a.m.
[url=synth://ashkettleministorage.synth/]Ashkettle Mini Storage[/url], off the industrial estate road. Come in the gate, park on the gravel, do not block the lane.

Nine units, rows B and G, sold under the lien statute on the order of the facility. Sold by the unit, not by the item.

How this works. I cut the lock, open the door, and you look from where you are standing. You do not go in. You do not touch anything. You do not open a box. You bid on what you can see from the doorway with your own eyes and whatever is behind that is also yours.

Winning bidder pays at the table, takes the unit broom clean inside 48 hours, and takes everything, including the mattress. There is always a mattress.

Personal papers, photographs and identification documents come back to the facility office by statute and are not yours. If you find them in a box, bring them to the office. I will be at the office.

The legal notice ran three weeks in the public notices at [url=synth://now.verityledger.com/]now.verityledger.com[/url], because the statute says the newspaper of record and nobody has gone back and looked at what that is now.

One of these units has been sublet by a person who is not the tenant of record. That is not my problem on the day, but it is going to be somebody's, and I have told the office so in writing.

[b]Terms.[/b] Cash only on a lien sale. No checks, no cards. No buyer's premium. Bring a lock.

[b]The property.[/b] Frame house, 1,140 square feet, two bedrooms down and one up, full basement, oil furnace put in 2011, roof 2016. Detached garage, 24 by 24, concrete floor, no water. 3.1 acres, of which about 2 acres is hay and the rest is the yard and the fence line. Septic. Well, and the well test is in the file at the office and you may read it before you bid.

The basement has taken water twice that the family knows about, in 1998 and in 2011, both times from the front wall. I am telling you that now rather than after.

[b]Real estate terms.[/b] 10 percent down in cash or certified funds the day of the sale, balance at closing within 45 days. Sold subject to the seller's confirmation, which means I can knock it down and the seller can still say no, and if that happens your deposit comes straight back. Taxes prorated to closing. Title through [url=synth://veritytitleabstract.synth/]Verity Title and Abstract[/url], deed recorded at [url=synth://verityclerk.gov/s/land-records]the county clerk's office[/url]. listings.title: Results — what I post, what I do not, and how to read a price
listings.body:
I post the hammer price off the clerk's sheet, a few days after the sale, once Jeanette has the book closed.

I do not post the buyer's name. Not here, not at the table, not on the telephone. People have asked me who bought their mother's ring and I have told them the same thing every time.

Prices below are hammer. They do not include the 10 percent. If you are using them to value something in your own house, add nothing and subtract your hopes.

A price is what one person paid, on one Saturday, in one county, in whatever weather there was. It takes two people who both want it to make a price. One person who wants it makes a bargain, and I have knocked down a $400 chest for $60 because the man who would have run it up was in the lunch line.

Sale sheets:

[list][*][url=/l/l-res-consign]Saturday September 12 — fall consignment, New Carrow Grange[/url][*][url=/l/l-res-ledbetter]Saturday August 22 — Ledbetter estate, Milbrook[/url][*][url=/l/l-res-dorrance]Thursday August 6 — Dorrance Township surplus, Bramwell Pike[/url][*][url=/l/l-res-kirchner]Saturday July 11 — Kirchner household, Gridfall[/url][*][url=/l/l-res-vandusen]Saturday May 30 — Van Dusen farm retirement, Coyne Flats[/url][*][url=/l/l-res-ordway]Saturday March 21 — Ordway, Marchfield[/url][/list]

Sheets older than that are in the binder at the office and you are welcome to sit down with it.

listings.title: RESULTS — Saturday July 11, 2026 — Kirchner household — Meacham Street, Gridfall
listings.body:
Moving sale, not an estate. The Kirchners are going to their daughter's in another state and had four rooms and a garage to clear.

131 lots, three hours ten minutes, 88 degrees in the driveway. Thin crowd. July is a bad month and I told them so in April.

[list][*]Sofa and chair, matching, good — $70[*]Dining table, oak, 6 chairs, 1 leaf — $155[*]Buffet, oak, matching the above — $90[*]Bedroom set, 1950s, 4 piece — $210[*]Bookcases, 3, pine — $18 each[*]Books, 14 boxes — $2 to $9 a box[*]Chest freezer, running — $45[*]Washer and dryer, both working — $130 the pair[*]Kitchen, 8 boxes, unsorted — $9 to $26[*]Cast iron, 6 pieces, one lot — $115[*]Pyrex, 2 flats — $85[*]Christmas, 11 boxes — $22 the lot[*]Riding mower, 2011, runs — $260[*]Snow blower, 2 stage, starts — $145[*]Hand tools, 6 boxes — $15 to $60[*]Ladders, 2 — $35 the pair[*]Patio set, table and 4 chairs — $50[*]Bicycles, 3, one flat — $28 the lot[*]Exercise bike — no bid[*]Tube television, 27 inch, in the cabinet — no bid[*]Encyclopedias, 1974, complete — no bid[/list]

The Pyrex brought more than the buffet. I have stopped predicting which way a Saturday will go on smalls.

The exercise bike, the television and the encyclopedias went in my truck to the transfer station on Monday at a cost of $31, which came off the settlement, which is why those three things are on the list of what I will not take.

listings.title: RESULTS — Thursday August 6, 2026 — Dorrance Township surplus — town shed, Bramwell Pike
listings.body:
Public surplus sale for Dorrance Township, by resolution of the board, at the town shed on Bramwell Pike.

41 lots, one hour fifty. Small crowd, which is what a Thursday in August buys you.

[list][*]1998 single axle dump truck, plow frame, 141,000 miles, runs — $3,100[*]Plow blade, 10 ft, off the above, sold separate — $425[*]Grader blades, 6, new in the crate — $210 the lot[*]Culverts, 4, 15 inch, used — $95 the lot[*]Sand spreader, tailgate mount — $180[*]Chainsaws, 3, two running — $115 the lot[*]Shop heater, propane — $60[*]Desk, metal, and 2 chairs — $15[*]Filing cabinets, 4 drawer, 3 — $22 the lot[*]Road signs, 14, retired, faces sanded — $9 to $31 each[*]Salt bin lids, 2 — no bid[*]Pallet of hydraulic hose fittings — $70[/list]

The township's legal notice ran in the public notices at [url=synth://now.verityledger.com/]now.verityledger.com[/url] with the date given as August 16. August 16 was a Sunday and there was no sale on it.

I put Terry at the end of the lane on the 16th with a folding chair to tell people. Nine cars came. Two of them had driven from the north end.

The township clerk sent the correct date to the paper twice and has the fax confirmations. She showed them to me. They are dated and they are right. [url=synth://thequarry.news/]The Quarry[/url] printed the whole business two weeks later, which is the only reason anybody outside the township heard about it.

listings.title: RESULTS — Saturday August 22, 2026 — Ledbetter estate — 3 Hoyt Road, Milbrook
listings.body:
Contents of the house and the two sheds, on the order of the executor. Alvin Ledbetter died in February. He was 88 and he had been in that house since 1961.

176 lots, three hours forty. 74 numbers issued. Hot, and the shade was all on the wrong side of the yard by eleven.

[list][*]Kitchen cabinet, painted, with the bin — $110[*]Chest of drawers, oak, 4 drawer, one runner needs waxing — $85[*]Bedstead, full, rails — $40[*]Rocker, caned, sound — $55[*]Kitchen table, porcelain top — $130[*]Crocks, 3, one bail handle — $185 the lot[*]Blue jars, 4 flats — $96[*]Cast iron, 9 pieces — $140[*]Churn, glass, lid cracked — $22[*]6 boxes, kitchen, unsorted — $19[*]5 boxes, bedroom, unsorted — $13[*]Linens, 2 boxes — $8[*]Quilts, 4, worn — $60 the lot[*]Sled, wood, painted — $45[*]Traps, 11, assorted — $75 the lot[*]Cross cut saw, 5 ft, 2 man — $65[*]Hand tools, 7 boxes — $14 to $48[*]Log chains, several — $55 the lot[*]Wheelbarrow, wood tray, sound — $90[*]Milk cans, 4 — $52 each[*]Fence stretcher and 2 post drivers — $35[*]Lawn mower, push, runs — $30[*]Tube television — no bid[*]Lot 88 — 1 box, photographs, unsorted — no bid[/list]

The milk cans were bid by people who are going to put flowers in them and by one man who is going to put milk in them, and the man who wanted milk in them stopped at $52.

About Lot 88, see [url=/l/l-lo-photos]the note in After the Sale[/url].

listings.title: RESULTS — Saturday September 12, 2026 — fall consignment — New Carrow Grange
listings.body:
Consigned by nineteen people. 246 lots, four hours five minutes. Inside, because it rained from nine until two.

[list][*]Pedal tractor, repainted — $180[*]Gun cabinet, oak, glass front, key — $145[*]Hand tools, 22 lots — $8 to $95[*]Cast iron, sold in 6 lots — $25 to $130[*]Blue jars, 7 flats — $31 to $70 a flat[*]Lumber, oak, 400 board feet, air dried — $310[*]Dining chairs, 6, pressback — $155 the set[*]Sewing machine, treadle — $45[*]Crock, 6 gallon, chipped — $95[*]Wagon wheels, 2, iron tyre — $120 the pair[*]Detecting finds, 3 lots, buttons and buckles — $14 to $60[*]Railroad paperwork, 1 box, waybills 1954 to 1971 — $85[*]Signal lantern, clear globe, no maker — $210[*]Crosscut saw — $40[*]Wood cook stove, complete, needs a grate — $275[*]Snowmobile, 1996, does not run — $130[*]Chest freezer, running — $40[*]Box lots, smalls, 48 of them — $2 to $18[/list]

The waybill box went to a man from the rail forum who read every sheet in it standing up at the preview and then bid on it like he had not.

The detecting lots came in from a man off [url=synth://gridfalldetectorists.net/]the detectorists' board[/url] who cleans things properly and labels where they came from. That doubles what they bring and I have told the rest of them so.

Two consignors withdrew items on the morning after take-in had closed. I sold them anyway, because I had already numbered them, and then I gave the money to the consignors, which is how that has to work and why take-in closes when it closes.

listings.title: After the sale — no-sale items, priced, at the office
listings.body:
What did not sell, with a price on it, in the pole barn on Grange Road. Saturdays 9 to 12, or telephone the office first and I will be there when you get there.

[list][*]Chest freezer, running, from the Kirchner sale — $40[*]Console radio cabinet, no tubes, Toomey preview reject — $25[*]Storm windows, 11, various — $1 each[*]Books, box lots — $2 a box, $35 the pallet[*]Aluminum lawn chairs, 4 — $20[*]Garden tools — $2 each, or fill a bucket for $10[*]Pump organ, plays, 3 stops stick — $150[*]Folding chairs, 74, from the church sale, available after November 9 — $2 each, $120 the lot[*]Salt bin lids, 2, Dorrance Township — free, take them[*]Mattresses — I do not have any and I will not have any[/list]

Prices come down on the second Saturday of the month and again on the fourth. After that it goes into the next consignment sale and I take my commission on it like everybody else does.

Somebody has my no-sale list on a shopping page with the prices multiplied by four and free shipping on the chest freezer. The chest freezer weighs two hundred and ten pounds and it is nine feet from where I am typing this.

listings.title: Lot 88, one box of photographs, no bid
listings.body:
Ledbetter sale, August 22. Lot 88 was one box, photographs, unsorted. I started it at a dollar and nobody put a hand up, which happens.

It is in the back of my truck.

There are people in it. Somebody wrote on the backs of some of them in pencil. There are names I do not know and one that says Kerrin school 1957, and two of a threshing crew with a steam engine in the background, and about forty that are somebody's holiday.

If it is your family, telephone the office and describe one photograph in it. You do not have to buy anything and I am not going to make you stand there while I decide whether I believe you.

If nobody comes by the end of November I will take the box to [url=synth://marchfieldlibrary.blog/]the library in Marchfield[/url] and let them decide what it is. They took four boxes off Mrs. Ordway in December and did not complain about it once.

This is the fourth box of photographs in three years. The other three are also in the barn.

listings.title: What I will take, what I will not, and what I charge
listings.body:
[b]Yes.[/b] Tools of any kind. Farm machinery that runs or is complete. Furniture that is not particle board. Crocks, jars, cast iron, quilts, signs, lanterns, anything with a maker's name cast into it. Guns, with a dealer at the table. Coins, if there are enough to be worth a case and a man to sit by it.

[b]No.[/b] Mattresses. Tube televisions. Particle board bedroom sets. Exercise equipment. Encyclopedias. Printers. Organs, unless it is a pump organ. Anything with a fuel tank I cannot see the bottom of. Paint, chemicals, and the half can of something in the garage with no label on it.

[b]It depends.[/b] Books. Pianos. China. Anything you have been told is valuable by a person who then did not offer to buy it.

[b]Commission[/b], out of the proceeds: 25 percent under $50, 15 percent from $50 to $500, 10 percent over $500, nothing at all on a lot under $5 because I put those in a box and sell the box. On a whole-house estate I quote a flat percentage after I have walked through it, and I walk through it for nothing.

If you have one good thing and not a houseful, you do not need me and you should not pay me. Put it in [url=synth://classifieds.verity.net/]the classifieds[/url], price it yourself and keep all of it. I will tell you that on the telephone and I have told about a hundred people that.

One more thing, because three families have asked me this year.

A man is going around the county offering a flat number for the entire contents of a house, sight unseen, cash, out by Friday. That is a real business and it is legal. If you are eleven hundred miles away and the house has to be empty, it may well be the right answer and I will tell you so.

It is usually not the right answer. Ask him what he does with it afterwards, and see whether he tells you, and see whether the number changes after he has been inside.

listings.title: Wanted for the November consignment sale — take-in closes Thursday November 5
listings.body:
Taking consignments through Thursday November 5 for the sale of Saturday November 14 at the Grange.

[b]Short of:[/b] hand tools, log chains, wagon gear, cast iron, blue jars, crocks, lanterns, anything at all with the branch line's name on it.

[b]Long on:[/b] dining chairs. I have thirty-one dining chairs in the barn. Do not bring me dining chairs.

Take-in is Thursday 1:00 to 6:00 and Friday 9:00 to 4:00, and take-in closes when it closes.

Walt Pennock asked to be telephoned if an antenna rotator ever came through. One did, in July. He was already standing there when it sold.

[url=synth://verityextension.org/]The extension office[/url] has asked me to say that they will not tell you what your tractor is worth and that this is not what they are for. I am saying it. They are right.

If you are clearing a house and you do not know where to start, telephone the office and I will come and walk through it. There is no charge for that and there is no obligation after it. I do about forty of those a year and take maybe half.
